confusions: SquareRange.from/to could denote either the two endpoints of a straight-line corridor (rank/file/diagonal) being highlighted for illustration, or a from-square/to-square pair mimicking a move; I picked the highlighted-line-segment reading since it's reused by RangeList and RangeWithPieces which read as visual/geometric annotations rather than moves.

WonSequence.game_points could mean chess.com match scoring points (0, 0.5, 1 per game in a match/tournament) or the material/centipawn-style point value gained at each step of a tactical sequence; I picked the material-tally-per-step reading since 'WonSequence' paired with a repeated list suggests a running tally of points captured through a combination, not match scores.

Classification as an empty message is ambiguous: it could be a real placeholder for future classification data, or purely a tag/marker whose only meaning is 'this event is a classification-type event' with all actual info carried elsewhere (e.g. an event-type enum outside this excerpt); I assumed the latter (pure marker with no payload).

DirectedRelation's origin/target oneofs are ambiguous as to whether origin is always the 'active' piece (attacker/defender/mover) and target the passive one, or whether direction is relation-specific (e.g. for RELATION_KING_ESCAPE the 'origin' might actually be the escaping king and 'target' the escape square, reversing the usual attacker->target flow); I assumed origin is consistently the acting/source entity and target the recipient across all Relation values.

guesses.expected_docstring: A straight-line segment on the board (rank, file, or diagonal) defined by its two endpoint squares, used to visually or logically denote a corridor of squares for annotation purposes (e.g. a rook's sweep line or a diagonal being highlighted).
The starting square of the line segment.
The ending square of the line segment.

An empty payload used purely as a type tag within the BoardEventProfile.profile oneof, indicating this board event is a general classification-type event with no additional structured data beyond what the event's own type/metadata already conveys.
Describes a tactical sequence that results in a net material (or evaluation) gain, capturing the point value won at each step of the sequence.
The material point values (e.g. pawn=1, knight/bishop=3, rook=5, queen=9) gained or exchanged at each successive step of the won sequence, in order.
A single square called out for annotation, e.g. a highlighted key square in the position being explained.
The square being marked/highlighted.
An unordered collection of squares grouped together as related locations of interest (e.g. a set of weak squares, outposts, or escape squares) with no implied piece occupancy.
The squares that make up this location set.

Describes a directed tactical or positional relationship between two board entities (each identified either by piece or by bare square), where the relation flows from an origin endpoint to a target endpoint and is classified by a Relation enum (e.g. attack, defense, pin-break).
The kind of directed relationship connecting the origin to the target.
The origin endpoint of the relation, identified as a specific piece (used when the acting entity is a piece rather than a bare square).
The origin endpoint of the relation, identified as a bare square (used when the origin is a location rather than a specific piece, e.g. an empty square a piece moves from or through).
The target endpoint of the relation, identified as a specific piece (e.g. the piece being attacked, defended, or checked).
The target endpoint of the relation, identified as a bare square (used when the target is a location rather than an occupying piece, e.g. a promotion square or king-escape square).
Default/unset value indicating no relation type was specified; should never appear in valid data.
The origin piece attacks (threatens to capture) the target.
The origin piece is offered as a sacrifice in relation to the target, typically allowing itself to be captured for a tactical or positional gain involving the target.
The origin piece moving out of the way reveals (discovers) an attack from another piece onto the target.
The origin piece delivers check to the target (the king).
The origin piece defends (guards) the target.
The origin piece removes (captures or deflects) a defender that was guarding the target, i.e. a 'removing the guard' tactic.
The origin (the king) has the target square available as an escape square to move to.
The origin piece's move breaks an existing pin that was constraining the target.
The origin piece develops (moves from its starting position) toward or into relation with the target square/piece as part of normal opening development.
The origin piece's forward advance is blocked by the target occupying the square in its path.
The origin pawn is running toward the target square, its promotion square, as part of a promotion race.
